name: Dom Perno
honors: High school All-America and MVP of the Connecticut state tournament as a Wilbur Cross senior
Two-time All-State at Wilbur Cross High School
Captain of UConn's 1963–64 NCAA Elite Eight team
bio: Dominic "Dom" Perno grew up in New Haven and starred at Wilbur Cross High School, where his teams won 49 consecutive games and he was named All-State twice; as a senior he was an All-America pick and MVP of the Connecticut state tournament. The self-described "little left-handed guard from Wilbur Cross" played three varsity seasons at UConn (1961–64), scoring 650 points, and captained the 1963–64 Huskies to the NCAA tournament's final eight. In the East Regional at Raleigh, North Carolina, he made two free throws with 32 seconds left and then stole the ball from Princeton All-America Bill Bradley to clinch a 52–50 upset.

After graduating in 1964, Perno coached at South Catholic High School in Hartford and then became athletic director and head basketball coach at St. Paul Catholic High School in Bristol. In August 1972 he returned to Storrs as an assistant to Dee Rowe, replacing Jim Valvano, and on March 17, 1977, after five seasons on Rowe's staff, he was named head coach.

His second team, led by freshmen Corny Thompson and Mike McKay, went 21–8, won the ECAC New England tournament and made UConn's first NCAA tournament appearance since 1976, losing 89–81 to Syracuse in Providence. It was the first of three straight 20-win seasons, and in 1979–80 UConn became one of the seven charter members of the Big East. Perno's teams played in the NIT in 1980, 1981 and 1982, and his rosters featured Thompson (1,810 career points and two first-team All-Big East selections), McKay, Kentucky transfer Chuck Aleksinas, point guard Karl Hobbs and New Haven's Earl Kelley, the 1982–83 Big East Rookie of the Year.

His last four teams finished with losing records (12–16, 13–15, 13–15 and 12–16). The 1985–86 team started 8–0 but lost its final eight games, seven of them after Kelley was ruled academically ineligible. On April 14, 1986, Perno resigned, effective immediately, with a 139–114 record. "I have concluded that this is the best decision for myself, my family, and Connecticut basketball," he said, adding that he had not been pressured out. His last roster included freshman Cliff Robinson, a future Huskies of Honor inductee, and UConn hired Northeastern's Jim Calhoun the following month.

Perno later served as vice president for sales and marketing at the Roland Dumont Group in Bristol and worked as a television analyst for the Big East Conference Television Network, for Hartford's WFSB-TV during the NCAA Tournament and for ESPN's international NBA broadcasts. He joined George Washington University's athletic department in November 1997 to run fundraising and marketing, was promoted to associate athletic director in 2006 and worked alongside his former point guard Karl Hobbs, GW's head coach from 2001. Perno retired from GW on June 30, 2011.
